children: Mitsubishi Motors Corp. on Wednesday unveiled the new version of the Pajero, a sports utility vehicle that was once a mainstay model of the Japanese automaker.

The fifth-generation Pajero will be released by March next year, the first time the model will be sold domestically in about seven years. The automaker halted production for domestic sales in 2019, and then in 2021, it halted production of vehicles made for export.
The new version maintains the popular features of its predecessors, such as off-road capability and durability, while adding a luxurious feel.

The latest Pajero can seat up to seven and has a diesel engine. Like older versions, it features a robust ladder frame chassis. It adopted T-shaped headlights — a departure from the round or square headlights typically seen on previous versions — to give it a more modern look.

To enhance off-road driving, the new Pajero features proprietary technology, which adjusts the car's wheels based on road conditions. It also includes multiple other features, such as a 14.3-inch monitor. The price will be announced at a later date.

It will first be released in Thailand — where the model will be produced — as well as Japan and Australia. It will go on sale within this fiscal year, which ends March 2027. Mitsubishi Motors plans to eventually expand sales to about 100 countries from the next fiscal year.

"The Pajero is a flagship model that best embodies the essence of Mitsubishi Motors," Keisuke Kishiura, president of the automaker, said at an event to unveil the new Pajero. "It is truly special for us."

The Pajero was first released in 1982. The model's sales increased steadily, boosted by a surge in leisure activities in Japan. Sales dropped as the leisure boom ended, and the automaker discontinued domestic sales in 2019.
However, Mitsubishi Motors decided to resume production of the Pajero, as outdoor activities have become popular again.
